content.text: I’ll check the current state of Makepad and GPUI and compare where each fits best.

input.input: text( await tools.web__run({search_query:[{q:"Makepad github README Rust UI framework"},{q:"GPUI gpui.rs Rust UI framework documentation"}],response_length:"short"}));

content.text:
**I’d pick GPUI for a desktop productivity app; Makepad for a visually experimental app that also needs web or mobile.** That’s my assessment of their current architecture and tooling.

| | Makepad | GPUI |
|---|---|---|
| UI authoring | Rust plus a live-editable UI scripting language | Rust views with fluent, CSS/Tailwind-like styling |
| Rendering | GPU 2D and 3D; strong emphasis on custom graphics | GPU UI; declarative views plus low-level custom elements |
| Platforms | Desktop, web/WASM, Android, iOS | Core documentation covers macOS, Linux/FreeBSD and Windows |
| Development feel | Visual experimentation through Studio and live editing | Application architecture through entities, views, actions and async tasks |
| Natural fit | Creative tools, animated interfaces, shader-heavy experiences | Editors, inboxes, workspaces, dense keyboard-driven tools |

Sources: [Makepad’s current README](https://github.com/makepad/makepad), [GPUI’s current README](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/gpui/README.md).

**GPUI’s advantage is its foundation for complex interaction.** It explicitly supports keyboard actions, shared application state, custom editor layouts, large lists and simulated-input testing. Its main cost is churn: it remains pre-1.0, and the maintainers warn of frequent breaking changes. [GPUI documentation](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/gpui/README.md)

**Makepad’s advantage is creative control across more targets.** Its live-editable language, Studio, and integrated 2D/3D rendering make it appealing when the visual experience is central to the product. The tradeoff, in my judgment, is learning more of Makepad’s own language and tooling. [Makepad](https://github.com/makepad/makepad)

GPUI also has a substantial component ecosystem: **GPUI Kit**—formerly the `gpui-component` repository—now advertises 75+ components, accessibility and WebAssembly support. Those are kit capabilities, so evaluate the exact stack rather than assuming core GPUI provides everything. [GPUI Kit](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit)

For a **native Baste studio**, I’d lean **GPUI** if the main experience is projects, candidate grids, inspectors and generation queues. I’d lean **Makepad** if an animated visual canvas and sharing the interface across desktop, web and mobile are central. Neither framework automatically produces a distinctive design; both give you control over that.
